main_text.p: infausto cursu reuocare. Hæc de Echneide fere omnia ex Plinio.
Cæterum in experimentis est, hirundinis cor palpitans deuoratum memoriam deperditam restituere, adque ingenium valere & intelligentiam.
Cor turturis viuum calensque comesum ad febres intermittentes omnes.
Anatem viuam ventri admotam compescere tormina.

Viuentem araneam iuglandis testis inclu-sam colloque subnexam pellere quartanam: ranarum oculos ante Solis ortum erutos, viuis illis in aquâ dimissis, alligatos, sicut & vnguiū præsegmina in pedibus & manibus febricitan-tis, cancri viui dorso superligata, cumq; eo in aquam fluentem proiecta, tertianas febres.
Talpæ viuentis dentem odontalgiam sanare contactu:
Officulum è poplite leporis nephritidi & spasmo flatulento.
Cor corui gestatum ad inhibendum so-mnum, cor vespertilionis ad eundem valere accersendum.
Ossa capitis equæ fugare erucas palo in hor-tis affixa.

page.notes: Faint show-through from the facing page is visible in the right margin and was not transcribed. The word "cacissime" at the foot is the catchword, shown in the body as the last line's continuation; the last line is printed as "cacissime" and may be read as a catchword. Possible doubtful readings: "vnguiū" and "Officulum" are as printed.
